full_judgment: 6. In our opinion this is a case in which on its appreciation in respect of the false embellishments made by the informant party in the statements of the witnesses we find that the statements made by the witnesses before the inquiring Magistrate clearly and manifestly failed to support the accusation against the accused petitioners. The contradictions and embellishments are so preposterous, that prolongation of the criminal proceeding against the innocent accused Zahirul Islam Chowdhury, Abdul Kader Chowdhury, Abu Bakkar Chowdhury and Shah Alam clearly amount to harassment and abuse of the process of the Court. In the case of T.N. Swami Vs. Amar Nath, 1950 Cr.L.J. 838 (Punj) it was held that criminal proceedings started on a complaint which did not contain any definite accusation against the accused petitioners amounted to an abuse of the process of the Court and in that case on that ground the criminal proceedings were quashed. It is not the case of the complainant that his first F.I.R. was not correctly recorded. When the complainant made no incriminating allegation against the said four accused persons prolongation the criminal proceeding against accused persons is an abuse of the process of the Court and the proceeding should be quashed
